items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: For as long as we draw breath we're migrating, and then at the moment of our death, we are reduced to bones in an instant. Thus, we take our people's bones with us wherever we move. It is our way.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: This wand not merely a tool to me.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: So then the bone came from ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: My clan mate's wing.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I learned how to carve from humans, so that I might make this wand.
He reads the old man's reaction, hoping he might capture some clue from his response.
The old man raises his eyebrows, mouth slightly open but wordless, eyes open and fixed straight on him. It is shock.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: My apologies, if I've caused offense. There may be cultural differences between us ...

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: So then you're a bone carver! What a surprise!

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: I know of a place that would be perfect for you!

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: It is called Nizhny Novgorod. Cool name, isn't it? There are many craftsmen there, and they make lions, tigers, reindeer, and even dragons out of bones! Their handicrafts are used as accessories on sheaths.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Can you imagine that? Legendary creatures coming to life through simple engravings on old bones ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Calm yourself, sir.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Otherwise, I think I may have to cast a calming arcane skill.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Oh, please! Don't worry. I'm totally fine. I'm not rabid! I'm only happy for you.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Ah, but I almost forgot, I promised to tell you everything, so I don't think you would like to see this false image anymore.

items.speaker: Lizheng
items.text: Please hold on a second.
A second later, the old man's image fades away like a drop of ink in water.
The face revealed beneath is surprisingly young.
He tidies up his appearance, already decent enough, and begins again more seriously.
Alright. Please allow me to introduce myself one more time.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You may call me "Leonid," "Hey, you," or "Employee," the name doesn't matter. Just pick one to make communication easier.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I work for the St. Pavlov Foundation. I don't think you would know of it, but it's an organization which provides support for arcanists and collects their information. So far it has helped countless arcanists.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I work at the Russian branch. Like the other branches, we are committed to helping arcanists. It's part of our duty.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: For example, if you are attacked by critters when you take a nap on the park bench, call us—but try to make sure you hadn't just drank too much vodka first.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: In truth, I love this job. It gives me the opportunities to get in touch with new things and people ...

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Like you, a rare case even among arcanists.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I owe you an apology, to be honest. We were going to catch those big critters with corn and wheat. You know, they haunt this place in winter. Never expected to see you here.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: We thought you were a new species, but you are … half man? So they called me here, just in case.
Gětiān has little sense of most of the technical jargon the now young man is speaking, but manages to capture the key information.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Please, you don't have to do anything. It was I who ate the crops without permission. I should repay you for them.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: So how much are they?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Oh, only a few Sharpodonties. It's already forgotten. Now back to bone carving, seriously ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Please ... wait. What is this "Sharpodonty"?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: A currency widely used by arcanists. I heard it has become popular even in the East now. Have you never seen one before?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: If you mean the things people use to "trade," the one I usually see is a round coin made of copper, with a hole in the middle. Though where I am from, many people simply barter.
They look into each other's eyes, each bewildered, not sure what to say next.
They're two very different creatures each from a very different culture.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Well, I'm not sure I see how to carry on our current conversation. Let's stop the Artificial Somnambulism and find another place to talk.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Please close your eyes ... I'll take you to a room where we can sit.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Alright.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: The corridors of our branch can be kind of narrow. You may find your wings brushing along the wall.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I will be careful.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I have another question.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: By all means, go ahead.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: It seems there is no language barrier between us. Is that part of your arcane skill?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: By the way, that grain you ate was soaked in liquor, you were passed out drunk when we found you. We mistook you for a strange critter, but then your wand glowed, my colleagues screamed as if a pack of bears or moose had broken loose in our branch again ...

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I had to confiscate it for now, and I took your pendant too, just in case.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I ... yes, our languages, it's my arcane skill working. I apologize for you finding me in that sorry scene.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: More than fine with it, our team didn't suffer any trouble, we've seen worse ... Ah! Here, we are.
The austere room places metal wherever one might expect wood, leaving the room with a monochromatic gray hue.
The layout imposes a feeling of strictness and cold.
Combing through the experiences he's witnessed through others' bones, Gětiān can only think of one place that would look this way.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Is this a prison?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Haha, you know, I told them to use more colors in the room, but they didn't listen!

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: This is, sadly, a bog-standard office of the Foundation. You've caught on to its biggest drawback—it does give the impression of a prison to anyone with even the slightest care for aesthetics.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Maybe it's to make us more eager in the field ... Who knows? Please take a seat.
He pulls out a chair for the bird, gesturing for him to sit, then sits on the opposite side.
Something round drops from between his fingers and onto the table.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: This is a Sharpodonty. Hold it if you want. Just be careful, it might bite you.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It looks similar to the coins I know, only without a hole in the middle.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It seems your kind have a preference for cats.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: It's a lion, a much larger animal! Imagine a cat larger than this table, with mane and a loud roar.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Hey!
Leonid grabs the Sharpodonty immediately and puts it in his pocket.
The pocket continues to make a racket of gnashing teeth and ineffectual anger.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: This is a splendid coin. It would be most difficult to steal.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Yes, though ... I never thought it would bite you. Usually Sharpodonties only bite humans or when irritated.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You look like a decent … bird.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I wonder if a lion likes being petted, like a cat does.
He admits to himself, frankly, that he likes being petted too.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You've come a long way from home though, that makes me think you're the curious type.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Now, before we move on, I must clarify that the Foundation does not intend to violate the privacy of any arcanists.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: The following questions are based on the information I have collected from the Artificial Somnambulism. It's a special circumstance and I hope you understand.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: To show my sincerity, here's your wand.
He takes out a long bone stick from a hidden place and pushes towards the awkwardly seated bird.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You've shown some trust in me, so I think I should trust you in return.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Few would close their eyes in front of an arcanist they just met without hesitation.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Your bones told me that you are a straightforward person, all deceptions aside.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: They also say there is something you want from me. That's why you are being so friendly.
Gětiān leaves the wand on the table, waiting for Leonid's response patiently.
After all, he received many such offers of kindness from the people beyond his mountain.
Whoever they were, they all shared one thing in common: there was always something they wanted.
There is always a motive behind a stranger's kindness.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: What do you want? Wealth, fame, social status, or a new arcane skill?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: People like you have similar purposes.
